samples.summary: `siblingsOf` was made context-aware, but the selection branch of `forEachBlockInSelection` still indexes `doc.document.blocks` with context-relative indices — Tab/indent in a header/footer with a multi-block selection mutates body blocks or throws
samples.evidence: The delta fixes only the cursor-only fallback (text-editor.ts:2869 `return this.doc.getContextBlocks()`). The selection branch bypasses `siblingsOf` entirely: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2831-2849` computes `startIdx/endIdx` with `this.doc.getBlockIndex(...)`, which resolves against `getContextBlocks()` (`packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:272` → `document.ts:158-161`, header/footer array when `doc.editContext !== 'body'`, set at `text-editor.ts:405`), then walks `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks` (line 2836) and calls `fn(b, topLevel)` (line 2849). With the caret in a header/footer and a range spanning two blocks, `applyListLevelChanges` (line 2712) therefore rewrites *body* blocks' `listLevel` (and `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` at 2754/2768 their `marginLeft`); if the header/footer region has more blocks than the body, `topLevel[i]` is `undefined` and `b.type` throws inside the keydown handler. The sibling implementation in `editor.ts` already does this correctly — `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1689-1702` uses `doc.getContextBlocks()` for the same branch — so text-editor.ts is now the only inconsistent copy. The new test (`editor-tab-bullet.test.ts:333-373`) exercises only the cursor-only path, so nothing catches this. Fix belongs at text-editor.ts:2836 (use `getContextBlocks()`).

samples.summary: New `markDirty` lookup uses the body-only `layout.blockParentMap` instead of the merged map, so a list item inside a header/footer table cell is marked dirty by its own id rather than its table's
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1609` reads `layout.blockParentMap` (body layout only). The merged body+header+footer map is built at `editor.ts:1573-1580` and published as `doc.blockParentMap` — every other cell-aware site in this file uses that one (e.g. `editor.ts:4041`, `editor.ts:4074`). For a header/footer cell block the body map misses, so `markDirty(change.block.id)` records a non-top-level id. Currently harmless (header/footer layouts are recomputed with `undefined` cache at `editor.ts:1540-1563`, and unknown ids are ignored by `computeLayout`), but it silently does nothing the moment header/footer layout gains an incremental cache.

verdict.reason: Verified directly in source. text-editor.ts:2831-2832 gets indices from doc.getBlockIndex(), which resolves against getContextBlocks() (document.ts:271-272 → 158-161: header/footer array when editContext !== 'body', set via setEditContext at text-editor.ts:405). Reachable: handleKeyDown's Tab case (1120-1122) → handleTab (2680-2705) → applyListLevelChanges (2712-2716) → forEachBlockInSelection, with no editContext guard; handleIndent/handleOutdent (2750-2778) the same. Consequence: planListLevelChanges (model/list-level.ts:97-118) groups by the handed sibling array and the ids of the handed blocks, so body blocks get setBlockType'd (2717-2722); if the header has more blocks than the body, topLevel[i] is undefined and `b.type` at 2839 throws in the keydown handler. editor.ts:1684-1702 does the same branch correctly via getContextBlocks() at 1689, confirming text-editor.ts is the inconsistent copy. Real, reachable, data-corrupting/crashing, and in the blast-radius lane (unupdated sibling call site violating the change's new context invariant).

finding.summary: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` returns the body-only `doc.document.blocks`, ignoring the header/footer edit context, so Tab / Shift+Tab / Cmd+] on a list item while editing a header or footer now plans no change at all (silent no-op where it previously worked).
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2865 `if (!info) return this.doc.document.blocks;` — but the doc's own accessor is context-scoped: packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:158-160 `getContextBlocks()` returns `header.blocks` / `footer.blocks` when `editContext !== 'body'`, and `getBlockIndex` (document.ts:271) is built on it. Header/footer editing is a live mode in this very class (text-editor.ts:403-406 `setEditContext`, 4580-4581 active layout, and `getCellInfo` at 3639-3643 deliberately uses the *active* layout). Because `planSiblingGroup` only emits changes for ids it finds inside the passed array (packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:64-84), a header list item handed the body array matches nothing and `handleTab`/`handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` become no-ops. The sibling implementation in editor.ts:1616 gets this right (`doc.getContextBlocks()`), which is the inconsistency. Same root affects the multi-block branch at text-editor.ts:2836 (`this.doc.document.blocks` indexed with context-scoped indices). Fix belongs on the new code: use `this.doc.getContextBlocks()`.

verdict.reason: The finding's headline and quoted evidence are stale/wrong: text-editor.ts:2869 already reads `if (!info) return this.doc.getContextBlocks();` (2865 is a comment, not the claimed `document.blocks` return), so the cursor-only Tab/Shift+Tab path in a header is NOT a no-op and the demanded fix is already applied. However, the same finding names a second site that IS present and real: text-editor.ts:2836 sets `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks` (body-only) while the indices at 2831-2832 come from `this.doc.getBlockIndex(...)`, which is context-scoped (document.ts:271-273 -> getContextBlocks(), document.ts:158-162). With a header/footer multi-block selection this indexes body blocks with header-relative indices, so applyListLevelChanges (2712-2723, reached from handleTab 2702 / handleIndent 2753 / handleOutdent 2767) plans list-level writes against the wrong region (or dereferences undefined if the body array is shorter). That path is reachable: header/footer drag selection exists (2224-2231) and non-body ranges are handled (3767); the parallel implementation in editor.ts:1689-1702 uses doc.getContextBlocks() in the identical branch, confirming the intended contract. Since refuting would drop a defect I verified at a file:line the finding itself cites, I confirm — but with low confidence, because only the text-editor.ts:2836 half of the finding stands; the siblingsOf claim is not-present.

finding.summary: Toolbar `indent()`/`outdent()` now mutate `listLevel` on subtree children that lie OUTSIDE the selection, but only walked blocks are passed to `markDirty`, so the incremental layout cache reuses those children's stale lines — text stays at the old indent while ordered-list numbering (recomputed from live blocks) updates, until some later edit dirties them.
finding.evidence: Incremental cache hit reuses lines laid out with the OLD list indent: packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:535-536 `} else if (canUseCache && !dirtyBlockIds!.has(block.id) && cache!.blocks.has(block.id)) { lines = cache!.blocks.get(block.id)!.lines; }` — the `effectiveBlock` with `marginLeft + LIST_INDENT_PX * (listLevel+1)` (layout.ts:493-501) is only consumed in the miss branch. `markDirty` is called only for blocks the walker visits (editor.ts:1698, 1707), and the un-selected subtree children are visited by neither walk. Unlike `toggleList` (editor.ts:3561) which calls `invalidateLayout()`, `indent()`/`outdent()` (editor.ts:3578, 3596) go straight to `render()` → `recomputeLayout()` with the partial dirty set (editor.ts:2246-2248, 1527). Meanwhile `computeListCounters` (layout.ts:1080-1099) reads live `block.listLevel`, so markers renumber while the text does not move. Fix on the new code: mark every planned block dirty in `applyListLevelChanges`, or call `invalidateLayout()` in indent/outdent.

verdict.reason: The finding's central premise — that `markDirty` is called only for blocks the selection walker visits, leaving out-of-selection subtree children with stale cached lines — is not true of this repository. `applyListLevelChanges` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1595-1612) iterates the full plan returned by `planListLevelChanges`, not the walk, and calls `markDirty(cellInfo?.tableBlockId ?? change.block.id)` for every change (editor.ts:1609-1610), with a comment naming this exact hazard. `planListLevelChanges`/`planSiblingGroup` emit a change entry for every subtree member from `i` to `end` (packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:76-81, 114-118), so the un-selected nested children are in `changes` and therefore in `dirtyBlockIds`. `indent()`/`outdent()` (editor.ts:3574-3589, 3590-3604) invoke `applyListLevelChanges` before `render()`, so by the time `recomputeLayout` passes `dirtyBlockIds` to `computeLayout` (editor.ts:1523-1532) the cache-hit branch at layout.ts:535-536 cannot fire for those children — they are in the dirty set and fall through to the miss branch that uses `effectiveBlock` with the new `LIST_INDENT_PX * (listLevel+1)` margin (layout.ts:492-502, 538). Table-cell children are mapped to `tableBlockId`, the same dirty-set granularity used elsewhere (editor.ts:1660, 1680, 1713). The layout-side half of the evidence checks out, but the bypass does not exist: the reviewer's proposed fix is already the implemented code.
